A1.justification: Both PDFs describe KIND and retain matching methods, experiments and results despite the revised title. All supplied pages are readable. v1 mentions an appendix but contains none; v2 includes Appendices A–B. Supplementary additions are assessed as newly documented in the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, baseline comparisons, component ablations and analyses of learngenes, including Tables 1–3.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and reports additional model-size comparisons, domain-shift experiments and per-task results in its appendix.

M1.justification: The factorized training, class gate and frozen-learngene/random-tailor adaptation remain. Section 3.4 adds a deployment procedure that selects relevant pretrained tailors and discards unrelated ones, enabling smaller models without further training. This extends deployment while retaining the core algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds generation experiments on CelebA-HQ, Hubble, MRI and Pokemon, substantially extending coverage beyond ImageNet to distinct visual domains. The ImageNet superclass construction, 150/461 class division and 18 downstream tasks remain.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds Laptop-diff to the model-size comparison alongside traditional pre-training and existing learngene methods. The original novel-class comparison retains all its comparators in v2 Table 2; LoHa and DoRA were already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: v2 introduces model-size construction comparisons and FDD evaluation for domain-shift tasks. Main-text pre-training changes from 200K to 300K steps, although Appendix Table 6 still specifies 200K. Table 7 revises v1's blanket fine-tuning learning rate for several baselines, and the reused sample-grid caption changes guidance from 4.0 to 3.0. These reported revisions do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 adds explicit tests of transfer under large domain shifts across four domains, substantially extending distribution-shift evidence. The original component ablations, convergence snapshots, knowledge-distribution statistics and with/without-tailor visualizations are retained rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions specify two seeds for the with/without-tailor visualization. Neither supplies quantitative repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or significance tests, and v2 introduces no new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds model-size results, four-domain FDD comparisons, per-task FIDs in Table 8 and supplementary generated samples. For example, Table 1 reports DiT-L KIND with 245.9M parameters and FID 9.33. v1 Tables 1–3 retain their numerical values as v2 Tables 2, 4 and 5, including KIND's novel-class DiT-L FID of 12.87.

T1.justification: The denoising objective, factorized weight representation and class-based component partition retain their mathematical substance. v2 expands the product into component notation and supplies pseudocode, but introduces no substantive new theoretical assumptions, propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion broaden the central contribution from transferable learngenes for efficient diffusion-model adaptation to decomposable pre-trained models supporting resource-constrained deployment and large domain shifts. Adaptive recombination of pretrained components becomes a principal claim, while the novel-class performance claim remains.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly qualifies when pretrained tailors should transfer: related tasks can reuse them, whereas large domain shifts may make their knowledge harmful, motivating random tailors instead. It also interprets recombination as avoiding repeated compression costs. The original explanations of class-agnostic learngenes and the class gate remain.

D1.justification: Appendix A supplies pseudocode, component counts, weight decay, DiT-block configuration, method/task-specific hyperparameters, downstream class assignments and superclass mappings. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation without establishing implementation changes. v2 also announces a future code release and provides its repository address; availability is not established by the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2.1 substantially repositions KIND around variable-sized model initialization, pruning and distillation, adding discussion of methods including Laptop-diff and LD-Pruner. v1's biological Learngene discussion is reduced, and new domain-shift and evaluation references support the broadened positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, method exposition and conclusion are extensively rewritten. v2 introduces a numbered section hierarchy, organizes results around deployment scenarios, removes the standalone baseline-description subsection and groups convergence with ablation analyses. The title and author list also change.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 3 are substantially redrawn, and Figure 2 clarifies pixel versus latent space. v2 adds comparison tables, a domain-shift image grid, appendix tables and sample galleries, while relocating retained displays and changing table highlighting. The retained tailor visualization's caption is corrected from 14 to 12 classes; its cases are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens evidence for transfer beyond ImageNet through four distinct domains and supports deployment claims with model-size comparisons. Its appendices supply important implementation and benchmark details missing from the supplied v1. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, particularly the conflicting 300K/200K pre-training budgets and changed guidance caption for identical samples, which still limit reproducibility.
